'''Jason Frederick Kidd''' (born March 23, 1973) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player. Widely regarded as one of the greatest [[point guard]]s of all time, Kidd was a 10-time [[NBA All-Star]], a six-time [[All-NBA Team]] member, and a nine-time [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] member. He won an [[NBA championship]] in 2011 as a member of the Dallas Mavericks and was a two-time gold medal winner in the [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympics]] with the [[United States men's national basketball team|U.S. national team]] in 2000 and 2008. He has been inducted into the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] twice: in 2018 for his individual career,<ref>{{cite news |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |last2=Haynes |first2=Chris |title=Jason Kidd, Steve Nash, Grant Hill to enter Basketball Hall of Fame |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22955081/steve-nash-jason-kidd-grant-hill-inducted-basketball-hall-fame |access-date=June 28, 2025 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=March 29, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/03/31/kidd-inducted-into-hof | title=Former Nets All-Star Jason Kidd Inducted Into Hall of Fame | website=NBA.com | date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> and in 2025 as a member of the [[2008 United States men's Olympic basketball team|Redeem Team]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Comeback story by Team USA's 2008 'Redeem Team' immortalized in Springfield |url=https://www.nba.com/news/redeem-team-hall-of-fame-feature-2025 |website=NBA}}</ref> In 2021, Kidd was honored as one of the league's greatest players by being named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]].<ref>Multiple sources:
* {{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/page/nbarankPGs/ranking-top-10-point-guards-ever |title=All-time #NBArank: Magic Johnson tops list of greatest point guards |date=January 12, 2016 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 22, 2022}}
* {{cite web |last=Bailey |first=Andy |date=September 11, 2019 |title=NBA all-time player rankings: Top 10 point guards |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2852716-nba-all-time-player-rankings-top-10-point-guards |access-date=September 11, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report |archive-date=January 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118182459/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2852716-nba-all-time-player-rankings-top-10-point-guards |url-status=live}}
* {{cite web |url=https://hoopshype.com/lists/20-greatest-point-guards-ever-the-hoopshype-list/ |title=20 greatest point guards ever: The HoopsHype list |date=November 3, 2021 |publisher=hoopshype.com |access-date=March 22, 2022}}
* {{cite web |title=NBA 75th Anniversary Team announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-75th-anniversary-team-announced |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=December 29, 2022 |date=October 21, 2021 |archive-date=October 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016202815/https://www.nba.com/news/nba-75th-anniversary-team-announced |url-status=live}}
* {{cite web |last=Daubs |first=Kyle |title=The greatest playmakers in NBA history |url=https://fadeawayworld.net/the-greatest-playmakers-in-nba-history |publisher=Fadeaway World |date=November 17, 2022 |access-date=November 17, 2022}}
</ref>

Kidd played [[college basketball]] for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] and was selected by the Dallas Mavericks in the first round of the [[1994 NBA draft]] as the second overall pick. He was named co-[[NBA Rookie of the Year]] in his first season with the Mavericks, along with Grant Hill. Then, from 1996 to 2001, Kidd played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] and later for the [[New Jersey Nets]] from 2001 to 2008. He led the Nets to two consecutive [[NBA Finals]] appearances in [[2002 NBA Finals|2002]] and [[2003 NBA Finals|2003]]. In the middle of the 2007–08 season, Kidd was traded back to Dallas. At age 38, Kidd won his only NBA championship when Dallas defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2011 NBA Finals]]. He finished his playing career in 2013 with the [[New York Knicks]]. 

Kidd's ability to [[basketball pass|pass]] and [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]] made him a regular [[triple-double]] threat. Upon his retirement, he ranked third in NBA history for career regular season triple-doubles with 107<ref>{{cite news | url=http://proxy.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310301020 | title=Jason Kidd's triple-double helps Mavs roll 76ers | date=March 1, 2011 | access-date=March 1, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120604110910/http://proxy.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310301020 | archive-date=June 4, 2012 | url-status=dead}}</ref><!--do not remove citation unless it is replaced with an updated one--> and third in career playoff triple-doubles with 11.<ref name="sec">{{cite web |publisher=ESPN | url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270512017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070520231207/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270512017 | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 20, 2007 | title=Nets control boards this time around, take Game 3 from Cavs | access-date=July 12, 2007 |date=May 12, 2007}}</ref> As of 2025, he ranks third on both the NBA all-time list in [[List of National Basketball Association career assists leaders|career assists]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/history/leaders/_/stat/assists|title=NBA History - Assists Leaders|website=espn.com|access-date=December 27, 2025}}</ref> and the NBA all-time list in [[List of National Basketball Association career steals leaders|career steals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/history/leaders/_/stat/steals|title=NBA History - Steals Leaders|website=espn.com|access-date=December 27, 2025}}</ref>

In June 2013, Kidd was hired as the head coach of the Nets, who had relocated from New Jersey to Brooklyn. After one season, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], where he coached for four seasons until he was fired mid-season in 2018. After a season off, he was an assistant coach for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], with whom he won an NBA championship in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]]; he reunited with the Mavericks organization in [[2021–22 NBA season|2021]] to become the franchise's head coach, reaching the Western Conference finals in his first season and reaching the [[2024 NBA Finals]] in his third season.

'''Jason Eugene Terry''' (born September 15, 1977), also known by the [[initialism]] '''JET''',<ref name=ovation>{{cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9084720|title=Dirk: Jason Terry deserves ovation|work=ESPN.com|date=March 22, 2013|access-date=March 26, 2020}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is an assistant coach for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played 19 seasons in the NBA as a [[combo guard]]. With the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Terry won the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] in [[2008–09 NBA season|2009]] and an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] in [[2011 NBA Finals|2011]]. A prolific 3-point shooter, Terry has made [[List of NBA career 3-point scoring leaders|the twelfth-most 3-point field goals]] in NBA history as of April 2026.<ref name=threes>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leaders/fg3_career.html|title=NBA & ABA Career Leaders and Records for 3-Pt Field Goals|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 21, 2019}}</ref>

'''Jason Anthoney Richardson Sr.''' (born January 20, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Richardson was taken by the [[Golden State Warriors]] as the fifth overall pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]] after playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. Richardson has also played for the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Orlando Magic]], and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].

Richardson is often remembered for his proficiency in dunking and shooting. Early in his career, he won the [[Slam Dunk Contest|NBA Dunk Contest]] in both 2002 and 2003, becoming the second player, after [[Michael Jordan]], to win the competition in consecutive years. Later, he became a more proficient shooter, leading the league in three-pointers made from the 2007–08 to 2011–12 seasons, with 820.<ref>{{cite web |title=Who led nba in total three pointers made from 2007-08 to 2011-12 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=who+led+nba+in+total+three+pointers+made+from+2007-08+to+2011-12 |website=statmuse |access-date=11 December 2024 |archive-date=January 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120105625/https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=who+led+nba+in+total+three+pointers+made+from+2007-08+to+2011-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> Since 2021, Richardson has been an active player for [[Tri-State (basketball)|Tri-State]] of the [[BIG3]].

In July 2025 he accepted an offer to become the top assistant coach for the [[Denver Nuggets]].
